children: Airline stocks were on the rise Monday alongside a 6% drop in Brent crude prices as the prospect of U.S./Iran negotiations to end the conflict eased concerns over oil supply disruptions and fuel costs.

are outperforming given their increased exposure to fuel costs.

Because lower-cost carriers have much leaner operating margins and with little to no premium revenue to provide a cushion to higher operating costs, these carriers are much more vulnerable to high fuel costs.

, the rise in jet fuel prices translated into an adjusted loss of $0.60 per share in the third quarter versus a loss of $0.40 in the same quarter last year, reflecting a 19.4% increase in cost per available seat mile (CASM) and 57% increase in average fuel prices.

With airline shares higher, the U.S. Global Jets ETF is up 4.5% on Monday, piercing the 50-day moving average for the first time since August and currently challenging resistance at the 200-day moving average.
